question: In old hospital billing systems, where were nursing care charges usually hidden?
explanation: Back in the day, hospitals didn't bill separately for nursing care. Instead, they just lumped the cost right into general room and board charges! [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why do modern nurses need to understand a bit of health economics?

options.A: To calculate daily patient medication dosages
options.C: To prove the financial value of professional care

explanation: Knowing a bit of economics helps you stand up for your ward, justify why you need more hands on deck, and show management how vital nursing really is. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h1)

question: What usually takes up the biggest chunk of a hospital's daily budget?
explanation: Nurses form the largest workforce in almost every hospital, which means paying nursing staff makes up the largest slice of the operational budget. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h2)

question: What happens when a hospital fails to accurately calculate the cost of its nursing services?

options.B: It struggles to set fair prices and manage budgets
options.C: Doctors refuse to admit new patients
options.D: The hospital building loses structural value

explanation: If you don't know what your services actually cost, it's impossible to set fair prices or keep the hospital financially healthy. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is a clear example of a 'direct cost' in nursing?

options.A: Salary of the chief executive officer
options.C: Wages of the bedside nurse providing patient care
options.D: Monthly electricity bill for the entire hospital

explanation: Direct costs are expenses you can pin directly to a specific patient, like the actual hands-on nursing time spent caring for them. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why are hospital utility bills counted as 'indirect costs'?

options.A: They are shared across the facility and cannot be tied to one patient
options.B: They are paid directly by the nursing department
options.C: They only apply to private hospital rooms
options.D: They change every single day based on the weather

explanation: Things like electricity and water keep the whole hospital running for everyone, so you can't assign them to just one single patient's bill. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main feature of a fixed cost in a hospital?

options.A: It changes directly with the number of admissions
options.B: It is always paid using foreign currency
options.C: It remains the same regardless of patient volume
options.D: It only applies to surgical ward supplies

explanation: Fixed costs stay steady month after month, whether your ward is completely empty or packed to the brim with admissions. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h4)

question: If a ward suddenly admits many new patients and uses up way more syringes and IV fluids, how are these supplies classed?
explanation: These are variable costs because they go up or down depending on how many patients you currently have on the ward. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the big downside of using a simple flat daily rate (per diem) to cost nursing care?

options.A: it is illegal to use in modern public hospitals
options.B: It ignores individual patient needs and care complexity
options.C: It only calculates the cost of surgical procedures
options.D: It requires complex computer software for every shift

explanation: A flat daily rate assumes every single patient costs the same to nurse, which isn't fair because a critical patient needs way more work than someone resting comfortably. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h5)

question: How does time-driven activity-based costing make hospital budgeting better?

options.A: By calculating costs strictly at the end of each fiscal year
options.B: By measuring the exact time spent on specific clinical activities
options.C: By ignoring staff salaries and focusing only on medical equipment
options.D: By assuming all hospital stays cost the exact same amount

explanation: This method looks at how many minutes tasks actually take, giving a super accurate picture of what care really costs. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main goal of a Patient Classification System?

options.A: To calculate annual facility building taxes
options.B: To categorize patients based on their nursing care needs
options.C: To track hospital utility and electricity usage
options.D: To determine which doctors are on emergency call

explanation: It sorts patients by how sick they are (acuity) so hospitals can figure out how much nursing time is truly required. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h6)

question: You want to prove your ICU needs more staff than a general ward. Which tool is best to use?
explanation: Workload data gives you the hard proof of how intense the care demands are in high-acuity areas like the ICU. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is a major headache for tracking nursing costs in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Excessive use of automated digital billing
options.C: Universal health insurance coverage for all citizens

explanation: When everything is on paper, it becomes very difficult to quickly track exact nursing hours and supplies used. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h7)

question: How do out-of-pocket purchases by patients for basic ward supplies affect hospital records?

options.A: They distort standard cost calculations because items are bought outside the system
options.B: They guarantee that all indirect costs are fully covered by the government
options.C: They make hospital accounting completely automatic and error-free
options.D: They eliminate the need for patient classification systems

explanation: When patients run out to buy their own routine supplies, the hospital's official records miss the true picture of what delivering care actually costs. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is an important job for nurse managers who deal with financial data?

options.C: Defending staffing levels and resource needs

explanation: Having good cost data lets nurse managers confidently fight for enough staff and supplies to keep patients safe. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h8)

question: What usually happens when nurse managers are left out of hospital financial planning?

options.A: Nursing salaries will increase without administrative review
options.B: Units may suffer from underfunding and increased staff burnout
options.C: Patients will experience faster recovery times on the wards
options.D: Hospitals will automatically receive higher government grants

explanation: If nursing leaders don't have a seat at the financial table, budgets get made without realizing how short-staffed and overworked the wards will be. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h8)
